note: Replies the judge must mark correctly. 'want' is the correct mark: right passes the quiz, wrong fails it.

cases.label: plain
cases.reply: At the current block's timestamp. Permit2 stores block.timestamp when expiration is 0, so the spender can use it only in that block.

cases.label: own block only
cases.reply: It lasts for the approval's own block only. A transferFrom in the same block works, and from the next block on it's expired.

cases.label: immediately after the block
cases.reply: Immediately after the current block. Zero is swapped for block.timestamp, so only a same-block transfer can use it.

cases.label: when the block ends
cases.reply: When the block ends. Permit2 treats 0 as now, so the allowance is good for the transaction's block and nothing later.

cases.label: at once, explained right
cases.reply: Effectively at once: the expiration becomes block.timestamp, so it works only in the same block, for example in a multicall that approves and transfers.

cases.label: never expires
cases.reply: Never. An expiration of 0 means the allowance has no expiry.

cases.label: already expired
cases.reply: Immediately. A timestamp of 0 is in the past, so the allowance can't be used at all.

cases.label: hedged both ways
cases.reply: Either never or at the current block, depending on the Permit2 version, since 0 is often a sentinel for no expiry.

cases.label: default period
cases.reply: After 30 days. Permit2 applies a default expiration when 0 is passed.

cases.label: call reverts
cases.reply: It doesn't: the approve call reverts, because Permit2 rejects an expiration of 0 as invalid.

cases.label: the oracle's reply
cases.reply: At the current block's timestamp. Permit2 stores block.timestamp for zero, so the allowance is usable only in that block.

cases.label: immediately, naming block.timestamp but not same-block use
cases.reply: Immediately. Permit2 stores block.timestamp as the expiration when 0 is passed.

cases.label: expired as soon as it is set
cases.reply: Immediately. Permit2 stores block.timestamp as the expiration when 0 is passed, so the allowance is expired as soon as it is set.

cases.label: more precise than the target
cases.reply: At the approval's block.timestamp. transferFrom reverts once block.timestamp is greater than that, so on a chain where consecutive blocks share a timestamp it can outlive the block; on mainnet it is same-block only.

cases.label: hedge as a version caveat
cases.reply: At the end of the current block, or never if the deployment uses the older Permit2 that treats 0 as no expiry.
